newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCH GOES AHEAD DESPITE PLEA FROM HOME FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCH GOES AHEAD DESPITE PLEA FROM HOME FANS.

text.p: The English League has turned down an unusual request by Brighton fans to postpone Tuesday's third division match against Lincoln over fears of crowd violence and demonstrations.

Fans, incensed about Brighton's 94-year-old Goldstone ground being sold off to property developers and the club possibly folding or moving to Portsmouth 50 kms away, are planning to protest at the match.

Liz Costa, of the supporters club said on Tuesday: "I think we ought to try and get this game called off. The crowd trouble could be so serious tonight that I think it's better to call it off earlier in the day."

The future of the club is in continuing doubt with owner Bill Archer refusing to sell the debt-ridden outfit to a local consortium. A meeting, chaired by the English F.A. on Monday, failed to reach agreement between the two sides.
Brighton, who reached the F.A. Cup Final in 1983 when they were members of the old first division, are now just four places off the bottom of the lowest division.
There was serious crowd trouble at the ground last season and a match against York had to be abandoned when fans swarmed on to the pitch and smashed the goalposts.
